steps: A begins against a stable committed snapshot S.
B commits changes after S without altering what A reads.
A writes based on its snapshot while reading repeatably.
Commit rejects direct write conflicts, though disjoint writes can still create write skew.

lesson.scenario: Two veterinarians independently take the last two surgeons off call, demonstrating write skew.
entities: stores Alice and Ben on-call flags
reads snapshot S=70 and updates Alice
reads snapshot S=70 and updates Ben
requires at least one surgeon on call

steps.title: Start from valid coverage
steps.narration: Both surgeons are on call when snapshot 70 is established.
steps.invariant: Each transaction reads one stable committed snapshot.

steps.title: Alice approves leave
steps.narration: Alice sees Ben on call and prepares to set only her own row to OFF.
steps.invariant: Reads do not change when concurrent transactions later commit.

steps.title: Ben approves leave
steps.narration: Ben sees Alice on call in the same snapshot and writes a different row.
steps.outcome: The transactions do not have a direct write-write conflict.
steps.invariant: Snapshot isolation commonly rejects concurrent writes to the same item, not disjoint items.

steps.title: Commit both disjoint writes
steps.narration: Alice commits at 71 and Ben commits at 72 because their write sets do not overlap.
steps.outcome: Write skew violates coverage despite repeatable reads and no dirty data.
steps.invariant: Snapshot isolation alone does not guarantee arbitrary cross-row invariants.

steps.title: Make the conflict explicit
steps.narration: A repair transaction restores Ben and future leave requests lock a shared coverage row.
steps.outcome: Materializing the invariant creates a write conflict that snapshot isolation can detect.
steps.invariant: Critical predicates require explicit locking, constraint design, or serializable isolation.

production.scenario: A retail checkout service reads cart, promotion, and stock state from one regional SQL cluster while staging an order attempt.
components: Boundary service that assembles cart, promo, and stock state
Black-box transaction manager for one checkout attempt
Authoritative carts, promotions, stock holds, and orders
Concurrent worker creating and releasing stock holds for other checkouts
Durable record of checkout attempts and outcomes
Worker that retries abandoned or conflicted attempts from the durable journal
flows: A customer confirms checkout for the current cart.
The boundary service creates a durable attempt record before it starts the transaction.
The API opens one checkout transaction tied to the durable attempt record.
read cart, stock, and promo snapshot
The transaction reads a single coherent view of the order-critical tables.
Other checkout workers concurrently create or release stock holds in the same cluster.
The final order outcome or conflict is durably written back to the attempt journal.
The retry worker looks for attempts that need replay after client disconnects or write conflicts.
Recovery can replay the checkout attempt against a fresh view without losing the original intent.
